title: Nuclear Fission and Fusion
text: Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy atomic nucleus (such as uranium-235) into smaller nuclei, releasing energy; it powers nuclear reactors and atomic weapons. Nuclear fusion is the combining of light nuclei (such as hydrogen isotopes) into a heavier nucleus, releasing even more energy per reaction; it powers the sun and stars. Fusion is considered a promising future energy source because it produces minimal long-lived radioactive waste, though sustained controlled fusion remains a significant engineering challenge.
